raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year. I'm 65, been working these 14 mu for 40 years, so I know every corner. My body isn't what it was, but my wife helps, and my daughter-in-law pitches in during garlic and wheat harvest. One son works construction in Handan and sends a bit back.

My layout hasn't changed much in years: 8 mu of wheat-maize rotation on the good land near the house, 4 mu of cotton on the lighter western plot (cotton tolerates that soil better), and 2 mu of garlic. I don't like switching things around — what works, works.

**Wheat (8 mu) — already in the ground.** I sowed in mid-October, Jimai 22 seed I get from the co-op. Before sowing I spread about 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu, that's my base, same as always. I did the winter water in early December when the ground was just about to freeze. In March when it greened up, I irrigated once and topdressed about 18 kg urea per mu. At jointing (early April, just finished) I sprayed for aphids and a bit of powdery mildew — one pass, mixed herbicide with it to save a trip. I'll water one more time at heading in early May if it stays dry. My yield target is around 450 kg/mu — I got 470 last year but weather was good, don't want to count chickens.

**Maize (8 mu, after wheat) — tight window.** After I combine the wheat in early June I have maybe 4-5 days to get maize in. I'll hire neighbor Old Wang's rotavator, then direct-seed Zhengdan 958 — reliable variety, everyone around here plants it. I put 35 kg of 15-15-15 in the row with the seed, and at big-bell stage in late July I side-dress about 15 kg urea. Usually one irrigation in July if rains are late. I'll spray once for armyworm and corn borer if I see them. Target 500 kg/mu.

**Cotton (4 mu) — planting in about a week.** Late April is the right time. I'll use a local improved variety, not those expensive Bt hybrids — at my scale the extra cost isn't worth it. Plow, rake, lay plastic film, transplant the seedlings I raised in the small nursery bed. Base fertilizer 35 kg compound, topdress 12 kg urea at budding in late June. Cotton is a lot of pesticide — 4 or 5 sprays for aphids, bollworm, spider mites through the summer. Irrigate once or twice depending on July-August rain. I'm only keeping cotton because I've done it forever and the land suits it. Price has been poor two years running, so if my son tells me to drop it next year I might listen.

**Garlic (2 mu) — nearly finished.** Sown end of September, covered with plastic. I put down 2 cartloads of farmyard manure per mu before planting plus 50 kg of compound fertilizer — garlic is a greedy crop. Topdressed urea twice over winter and spring, about 20 kg total. Watered three times already, need one more before harvest end of May. Sprayed once for leaf blight. Wife and daughter-in-law pull it, we hire 2 day-laborers for the heavy digging. Price was 4 yuan/jin last year, hope for similar.

Total input cost this year should run around 11,000 yuan. I keep 2,000 aside for surprise pesticide needs — two summers ago armyworm came bad and neighbors who didn't have cash lost half their maize.
